message.content:
Sure! Here’s a sample 7‑day itinerary for a memorable trip to Paris. Feel free to tweak dates, activities, or budget based on your preferences.

---

## 1️⃣ Trip Overview

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Duration** | 7 days (including travel) |
| **Travel Dates** | 15 – 21 July 2026 (adjust as needed) |
| **Estimated Budget** | €1,200 – €1,800 per person (mid‑range) |
| **Accommodation** | 3‑star boutique hotel or Airbnb in Le Marais or Saint‑Germain |
| **Transportation** | Round‑trip flight + public transit (Metro & RER) + occasional taxi/Uber |

---

## 2️⃣ Flights

| Segment | Suggested Airlines | Approx. Cost (per person) |
|---------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| Outbound | Air France, KLM, or Delta (direct or one‑stop) | €250 – €350 |
| Return | Same carrier | €250 – €350 |
| **Total** | | **€500 – €700** |

> *Tip:* Book 2–3 months in advance and use fare alerts (Google Flights, Skyscanner). Consider flying into Charles de Gaulle (CDG) for better international connections; you can take the RER B to central Paris.

---

## 3️⃣ Accommodation (7 nights)

| Option | Example Property | Approx. Cost (per night) | Total |
|--------|------------------|--------------------------|-------|
| Boutique Hotel | Hôtel Le Six (Le Marais) | €140 | €980 |
| Airbnb | 1‑bedroom loft in Saint‑Germain | €120 | €840 |
| Mid‑Range Hotel | Hotel Ekta (Champs‑Élysées) | €130 | €910 |

> *Tip:* Look for properties with free Wi‑Fi, a kitchenette, and a good location near Metro stops. Booking.com or Airbnb often offer free cancellation for added flexibility.

---

## 4️⃣ Daily Itinerary

| Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening |
|-----|---------|-----------|---------|
| **Day 1** | Arrive CDG → RER B to Gare du Nord → Check‑in | Explore Le Marais: Place des Vosges, Musée Picasso | Dinner at Le Coupe Chou (classic French) |
| **Day 2** | Louvre Museum (early entry) | Walk along Seine → Île de la Cité → Notre‑Dame | Seine river cruise (night) |
| **Day 3** | Eiffel Tower (skip‑the‑line ticket) | Picnic at Champ de Mars | Montmartre: Sacré‑Coeur, Moulin Rouge (optional show) |
| **Day 4** | Day trip to Versailles (RER C) | Palace & Gardens | Return to Paris → Café de Flore |
| **Day 5** | Musée d’Orsay | Lunch at Les Deux Magots | Opera Garnier tour |
| **Day 6** | Day trip to Giverny (Claude Monet’s house) | Explore Giverny village | Back to Paris → Wine tasting at La Cave à Vin |
| **Day 7** | Shopping on Rue Saint‑Honoré | Visit Palais Garnier or Musée Rodin | Farewell dinner at Le Jules Verne (Eiffel Tower) |

> *Optional:* Replace day trips with a visit to Disneyland Paris or the Champagne region if you prefer a different experience.

---

## 5️⃣ Transportation Within Paris

| Mode | Cost (per person) | Notes |
|------|-------------------|-------|
| Metro & RER | €1.90 per single ride | Or purchase a 10‑ride carnet (€16.90) |
| Unlimited 48‑hour pass | €14.50 | Good for heavy usage |
| Unlimited 72‑hour pass | €20.80 | Ideal for 3‑day stays |
| Taxi/Uber | €30–€40 per ride (short distance) | Use for airport transfers or late‑night returns |
| Bicycle rental (Velib) | €1.75 per hour | Great for short trips |

> *Tip:* Buy a Navigo Week Pass (€22.80) if you’re staying a full week; it covers unlimited travel on all public transport within zones 1‑5.

---

## 6️⃣ Dining & Food

| Category | Suggested Places | Approx. Cost (per person) |
|----------|------------------|---------------------------|
| Breakfast | Café de Flore, Ladurée | €8–€12 |
| Lunch | Bouillon Chartier (budget) | €10–€15 |
| Dinner | Le Jules Verne (Eiffel Tower) | €70–€100 |
| Snacks | Crêperie Breizh Café | €5–€8 |
| Coffee | Café Angelina | €6–€9 |

> *Tip:* Try local specialties: croissants, escargot, coq au vin, macarons, and cheese platters. Reserve tables in advance for popular spots.

---

## 7️⃣ Budget Breakdown (per person)

| Category | Cost |
|----------|------|
| Flights | €600 |
| Accommodation | €840 |
| Transport (public + taxis) | €150 |
| Food & Drinks | €300 |
| Attractions & Tours | €200 |
| Miscellaneous (souvenirs, tips) | €100 |
| **Total** | **€2,190** |

> *Note:* Prices vary by season and availability. Adjust by choosing cheaper dining options or fewer paid attractions.

---

## 8️⃣ Packing Checklist

| Item | Why |
|------|-----|
| Comfortable walking shoes | Paris is best explored on foot |
| Light rain jacket | Weather can be unpredictable |
| Power adapter (Type C/F) | For charging electronics |
| Reusable water bottle | Stay hydrated |
| Small daypack | Carry essentials during day trips |
| Travel insurance | Covers medical emergencies & trip cancellations |

---

## 9️⃣ Final Tips

1. **Book tickets in advance** for major attractions (Louvre, Eiffel Tower, Versailles) to avoid long queues.
2. **Use the Paris Pass** if you plan to visit many museums; it offers skip‑the‑line access and includes public transport.
3. **Learn basic French phrases** (“Bonjour”, “Merci”, “Au revoir”) – locals appreciate the effort.
4. **Stay flexible** – keep a backup plan for rainy days (museums, cafés, indoor markets).
5. **Enjoy the small moments** – a stroll through a hidden courtyard, a street performer, or a quiet café can be the highlight of your trip.

---

Let me know if you’d like help booking flights, hotels, or tickets, or if you have specific interests (art, food, history) so I can tailor the itinerary further!
